incident_found_during_this_stage.what: global_index/preflight_state.json and global_index/maxhold_state.json were both overwritten with a single Sunday key {"2026-08-23": true}
incident_found_during_this_stage.when: 2026-08-23 20:03:21, both files in the same second
incident_found_during_this_stage.who: a probe in MY previous turn's legacy->Track1 audit. It fired job_preflight() and job_maxhold() to capture their argv with _run patched, but did not redirect the state-file writers, so the real writers ran against a cleared in-memory dict
incident_found_during_this_stage.not_the_scheduler: scheduler_0821.log shows the last real pre-flight on 2026-08-21 and the next scheduled run as 2026-08-24; the job is mon-fri and 2026-08-23 is a Sunday
incident_found_during_this_stage.correction: the no-side-effects statement in scratch/track1_legacy_to_track1_full_route_audit_20260823.md is WRONG and is corrected by this entry
incident_found_during_this_stage.lost: the real weekday records, at minimum 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-21
incident_found_during_this_stage.live_impact_now: none — the running scheduler (pid 36656) loaded the file at startup on 2026-08-20 and holds the full dict in memory; _load_preflight_state is called only in main()
incident_found_during_this_stage.self_heal: Monday 2026-08-24 13:45 the live process writes its own in-memory dict back out, which restores the real records - PROVIDED the scheduler is not restarted before then
incident_found_during_this_stage.if_restarted_first: the Monday NKD night slots 01:10-02:55 read the previous business day (2026-08-21), find no record, and fail closed - every night slot skipped. Safe direction, but silent
incident_found_during_this_stage.not_repaired_by_me: writing True for a day I did not observe would be fabricating the fail-closed evidence the record exists to hold. The 2026-08-21 pre-flight IS attested by scheduler_0821.log, so a repair is reconstructable - it is the operator's call, and it races the running process
